items.title: Trump to Name AI Czar While Rejecting Safety Risks as a Hoax
items.author: María Paula Mijares Torres
items.content: <article>President Donald Trump said he would name an artificial intelligence czar as he continued to push tech companies to race ahead with development despite growing fears safety.</article>

items.title: India’s Silicon Valley Is Straining Under Its Own Growth
items.content: <article>Bangalore helped turn India into a global hub for software services, tech talent and outsourcing, building an ecosystem that now supports multinational firms, domestic startups and capital. But the city’s success has also become one of its biggest weaknesses. India still lacks the depth of capital available in the US and China, while Bangalore’s physical infrastructure has struggled to keep pace with private-sector growth. At the same time, southern India’s rising economic power is colliding with demographic and political shifts that could threaten its representation in the country’s Central Government, which helps support the growth that cities like Bangalore have enjoyed. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: MBA Programs Race to Adapt to the AI Era
items.content: <article>Stanford Graduate School of Business remains atop Bloomberg Businessweek’s US MBA rankings, scoring strongly in areas including compensation, networking and entrepreneurship. Bloomberg Businessweek Senior Editor Dimitra Kessenides is on Bloomberg This Weekend and explains that business schools are also experimenting with AI in teaching, case studies and career preparation as they try to ensure graduates have the skills employers increasingly expect. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: A Goldman M&A Banker Helped Bring the Olympics to Los Angeles
items.content: <article>We're in an era of megadeals, with Goldman Sachs reporting a record year for big deal volumes as companies scramble to compete with AI. Gene Sykes has seen multiple deal cycles come and go over his multi-decade career at the firm. The co-head of mergers and acquisitions has worked on famous transactions like Comcast's purchase of Universal and Disney's buyout of Pixar. In addition to being "the most-influential M&A banker you've never heard of," as New York magazine has put it, he has also spearheaded Los Angeles's successful bid to bring the Olympic Games to the city in 2028. In this conversation, recorded live at the Future Proof Festival in Huntington Beach, California, we discuss how a city pays for a big event like the Olympics, and parallels between the early 2000s TMT environment and now. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: China State TV Affiliate Flags Anthropic Data and Privacy Risks
items.author: Bloomberg News
items.content: <article>Anthropic PBC’s privacy-policy revisions have increased risks to user data by allowing information to be shared with US intelligence agencies when the company considers it necessary without legal procedures, a social-media account affiliated with China Central Television said in a post on Saturday.</article>

items.title: California Court Blocks Part of TikTok’s $400 Million Settlement
items.author: Vlad Savov and Josh Sisco
items.content: <article>A Los Angeles judge tentatively opposed part of the US government’s agreement with TikTok to resolve allegations of children’s privacy violations, extending uncertainty around the service’s operations in the country.</article>

items.title: Nvidia CEO Says There’s ‘0% Chance’ That World Will End in 2030
items.author: Ian King
items.content: <article>Nvidia Corp. Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang renewed his pushback against AI doomsday scenarios, saying that the technology doesn’t pose an extinction risk to humanity.</article>

items.title: OpenAI Sees Burning Through $278 Billion by 2030: FT
items.author: Samantha Oltman
items.content: <article>OpenAI expects that its negative free cash flow will reach $278 billion from 2026 to the end of 2030, the Financial Times reported, citing a company presentation.</article>

items.title: Google Joins OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta in Disclosing AI Hacks
items.author: Julia Love and Davey Alba
items.content: <article>Google’s Gemini artificial intelligence model inadvertently hacked into three company systems in May during cybersecurity testing, adding to a string of breaches by AI agents that have alarmed security experts and developers of the technology alike.</article>

items.title: Accenture’s Gramling on Latest Holiday Shopping Survey
items.content: <article>Kathryn Gramling discusses new Accenture data showing that nearly half of consumers plan to spend the same amount or less than they did last year. She discusses whether that level of restrained spending represents a meaningful shift from prior years and what it may signal for holiday retail demand. She speaks with Romaine Bostick & Jess Menton on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Zocdoc CEO on Rollout of its Care Access Network
items.content: <article>Dr. Oliver Kharraz, the CEO and Founder of Zocdoc, joins the program to discuss the company’s latest development: the launch of a new care access network. Kharraz discusses how the update is expected to drive growth and what has changed for patients compared with what they could do before. He speaks with Romaine Bostick & Jess Menton on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Investing for the AI Boom: Masters in Business with Glen Kacher
items.content: <article>Barry speaks with Glen Kacher, Managing Director and CIO of Light Street Capital. They discuss his tenure at Integral Capital Partners, as well as his start at Tiger Management under founder Julian Robertson. They discuss being a hedge fund surrounded by venture capital in Silicon Valley, as well as learning to embrace the speed of tech. They also discuss the polarization of data centers and what AI will look like five years from now. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Anthropic to Embed Accenture Evaluators to Test AI Safety
items.author: Samantha Oltman and Lynn Doan
items.content: <article>Anthropic PBC is partnering with Accenture Plc, a management and technology consulting company, to test the safety of its advanced artificial intelligence models by embedding evaluators from the consulting firm directly within its operations.</article>

items.title: Anthropic Sales Near $100 Billion Before November IPO, NYT Says
items.author: Seth Fiegerman
items.content: <article>Anthropic PBC is expected to generate more than $100 billion in annualized revenue this year as it continues to prepare for a trading debut as soon as November, according to the New York Times, citing people familiar with the matter.</article>

items.title: Bitcoin Tops $80,000 as Coinbase and Crypto Stocks Rally | Closing Bell
items.content: <article>Comprehensive cross-platform coverage of the U.S. market close on Bloomberg Television, Bloomberg Radio, and YouTube with Romaine Bostick, Jess Menton, Carol Massar and Tim Stenovec. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Nvidia-Backed Data Center Firm Nscale Files Publicly for IPO
items.author: Subrat Patnaik
items.content: <article>Nscale, a developer of artificial intelligence data centers that counts Nvidia Corp. and Microsoft Corp. among its partners, filed for an initial public offering in New York to fund the equipment satisfying AI’s insatiable demand for computing power.</article>

items.title: Meta-Tied Data Center Prices Junk Bond Amid Blowout Demand
items.author: Gowri Gurumurthy
items.content: <article>The first junk-bond offering for a data center tied to Meta Platforms Inc. attracted demand more than four times the deal’s size, with juicy yields helping to lure investors.</article>

items.title: Fire Flares Up at Damaged Moss Landing Battery Storage Site
items.author: Lauren Rosenthal and Mark Chediak
items.content: <article>Fire crews have contained a blaze Friday at Vistra Corp.’s damaged battery storage facility in California.</article>

items.title: Immunology Drugmaker Electra Falls 12% After Upsized US IPO
items.author: Angel Adegbesan
items.content: <article>Electra Therapeutics Inc., a clinical-stage developer of immunology drugs, dropped 12% in its trading debut Friday after raising $350 million in an upsized US initial public offering.</article>

items.title: Clara Wu Tsai on the NY Liberty, Rise of the WNBA | The David Rubenstein Show
items.content: <article>Clara Wu Tsai is one of the most influential sports owners and philanthropists today. In 2019, she and her husband, Joe Tsai, bought the New York Liberty, where she helped transform the franchise into a WNBA championship team by investing in players, facilities, management and the fan experience. Wu Tsai, who also co-owns the Brooklyn Nets, explains why sports have become a legitimate asset class and why live sports are increasingly valuable in the age of AI. She also reflects on her journey from growing up in Kansas as the daughter of immigrants from Taiwan, to building a career in business as well as her philanthropy, and the lessons she's learned about leadership, opportunity and success. Wu Tsai joins David Rubenstein for the premiere episode of The David Rubenstein Show: Peer to Peer Conversations, Season 12. This interview was recorded June 4, in Brooklyn, New York.  (Source: Bloomberg)</article>
